questions.stem: A 65-year-old man presents to his primary care doctor complaining of difficulties with his vision, particularly at night. The blurred vision is primarily in the right and left peripheral fields. He has myopia and wears corrective lenses. The physical examination reveals visual acuity of 20/100 bilaterally with visual field deficits on the right and left periphery. Where is the cranial lesion that results in bitemporal hemianopia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Optic chiasm
  • Lesions that affect the optic chiasm affect both of the peripheral visual fields, sparing the midline visual fields.
  • An example of this type of lesion would be a pituitary tumor that compresses the optic chiasm. A lesion in an optic nerve will result in blindness in the ipsilateral eye, and a lesion in an optic tract will result in homonymous hemianopia.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 171–172, 183–184.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman who complaints of slowly progressive loss of vision on her right side affecting both eyes are seen by her neurologist. A CT scan demonstrates a high-density space-occupying lesion. The lesion produces the visual field defect by compressing which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
The left optic tract
  • The loss of vision on one side of the visual field is called hemianopia. If it affects the same half of the visual field on both eyes, it is called homonymous hemianopia.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 164–165.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man sees his ophthalmologist because it is becoming increasingly difficult for him to read the newspaper. His vision problem most likely results from an inability to contract which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
The ciliary body
  • Contracting the ciliary body increases the refractive power of the eye for near vision.
  • The ciliary body is a ring-shaped structure located in the eye, just behind the iris. It is responsible for controlling the shape of the lens, which is necessary for focusing on near objects. The ciliary body contracts during the near vision, which causes the suspensory ligaments to relax and the lens to become more spherical, increasing its refractive power.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 188, 189.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man presents with a chief complaint of night blindness (nyctalopia). He is found to have avitaminosis A, which underlies the impairment of rod function. Which of the reactions in the retinal rods is caused directly by the absorption of light energy?

options.label: C
options.text: Transformation of 11-cis retinal to all-trans retinal

options.label: D
options.text: Transformation of metarhodopsin to lumia rhodopsin

questions.answerText: Transformation of 11-cis retinal to all-trans retinal
questions.solutionHtml:
Transformation of 11-cis retinal to all-trans retinal

The light-sensitive chemical in the retinal rods is called rhodopsin. It is a combination of 11-cis retinal and opsin.



Parson’s diseases of the eye, 22nd edition, Page number: 21, 218, 572.

questions.stem: While seeing a color chart a color-blind male has decreased vision for red light color which appears very light than that of other colors. Which of the following is the likely anomaly in him?
questions.solutionHtml:
Protanomaly

Protanomaly is the likely anomaly in the color-blind male described.



Ganong’s review of medical Physiology; 26th edition; page number: 197
